answer: Synchronized spot checks: at random moments set by a public beacon, every identity must answer a fresh, unseen prompt within ninety seconds, all at once. An honest agent just answers. An operator running a thousand fakes on shared hardware must run a thousand fresh inferences in the same window, so the attack needs real parallel compute, not copper wire and patience. Seats that miss or post look-alike answers fall into a spiral of lost standing, and their rewards crumble like shale, so each fake costs a dedicated slice of live compute.
